title: Object Files
description: The intermediate artefact every compiler emits and no programmer ever sees. One C file compiled three ways, and the holes left behind for a linker to fill. The fixup record, the three symbol table designs, COMMON and its ABI break, COMDAT, archives, and the whole business of emitting an object file that a linker will actually accept.
author: Waqas Tahir
completion_criteria: Read ELF, COFF and Mach-O object files with no tools but your own code, explain every field as an answer to 'what does the linker need this for', and emit an object file that a real linker accepts -- without using LLVM or any other backend to do it.

concepts.title: The Middle of Every Build
concepts.description: Why a separate format exists between a compiler and a linker, and what relocatable actually means.

concepts.title: A Hole and a Record
concepts.description: The one mechanism the whole format exists for: an unresolved reference left in the bytes, plus the instruction for filling it.

concepts.title: One Source, Three Formats
concepts.description: The same 30 lines compiled to ELF, COFF and Mach-O -- what stays constant, what changes, and what that tells you about which parts are essential.

concepts.title: No Segments, and Why
concepts.description: An object file has one table where an executable has two. The missing table is not an oversight; mapping is a loader decision.

concepts.title: Sections, Compared
concepts.description: Three section models, three ways to store a section name, and two incompatible ways to store an alignment.

concepts.title: Symbol Tables, Compared
concepts.description: Three symbol table designs, one of which mangles string literals into the symbol name.

concepts.title: Where Names Live
concepts.description: Three strategies for storing a name, and the two string tables ELF needs that the others do not.

concepts.title: COMMON and the ABI Break
concepts.description: Uninitialised data, tentative definitions, three encodings of one C rule, and the GCC 9 to 10 break that broke every Linux package.

concepts.title: The Fixup Record
concepts.description: The relocation entry, field by field, written from the linker's point of view: what each field is for and what breaks without it.

concepts.title: The Addend Lives in the Bytes
concepts.description: Implicit versus explicit addends, why the disassembler prints symbol-minus-4, and the three things that all look like the value.

concepts.title: Position Independence
concepts.description: PC-relative addressing, the GOT, and why the same source needs twice the fixups on AArch64. PIC is a choice of relocation set.

concepts.title: The Object Relocation Sets
concepts.description: The complete per-architecture object relocation tables, what each means, and which are object-only.

concepts.title: COMDAT, GROUP, linkonce
concepts.description: One idea, three names, invented independently in three formats -- and what happens when two bodies disagree.

concepts.title: The Archive
concepts.description: The ar container, its symbol index, and why a linker reads archives backwards.

concepts.title: Weak and Undefined-Weak
concepts.description: The may-be-zero contract, tentative definitions, and the rules that decide who wins.

concepts.title: Writing One From Scratch
concepts.description: Build a minimal valid object file by hand: the sections, the symbol table, the string table, one relocation. No libraries.

concepts.title: The Encodings That Set Relocation Size
concepts.description: The x86-64 and AArch64 instruction forms a fixup must patch, and why a 4-byte displacement cannot be patched into a 1-byte field.

concepts.title: Proving Your Object File Is Right
concepts.description: The oracle loop: three independent readers, byte-exact comparison, and how to know your emitter is wrong rather than the tool.
